three-sisters-agriculture.name: Three Sisters
three-sisters-agriculture.summary: A companion-planting method combining maize, beans and squash, in which each crop supports the others, developed by Indigenous peoples of the Americas.

hohokam.name: Hohokam
hohokam.summary: A culture of the North American Southwest, in south-central Arizona and Sonora, Mexico, that existed from about 300 to 1500 CE and is known for large-scale irrigation canals.

cahokia.name: Cahokia
cahokia.summary: The largest Native American city north of Mexico, inhabited from about 1050 to 1350 CE near present-day St. Louis, with around 120 earthworks and a peak population of up to 20,000.

mississippian-period-archaeology.name: Mississippian period
mississippian-period-archaeology.summary: An archaeological era (roughly 10th–16th centuries) in the Southern and Eastern United States marked by maize farming, population centers, and large platform mounds.

eastern-agricultural-complex.name: Eastern Agricultural Complex
eastern-agricultural-complex.summary: One of about ten independent centers of prehistoric plant domestication, in the woodlands of eastern North America, with cultivation beginning around 5300 BCE.

effigy-mound.name: Effigy Moundbuilder culture
effigy-mound.summary: Native American culture, mainly dated to 550–1200 CE, that built raised earthen mounds shaped like animals and figures across the upper Midwest.

basketmaker-culture.name: Basketmaker culture
basketmaker-culture.summary: A prehistoric culture of the pre-Ancestral Puebloans in the American Southwest, lasting from about 1500 BCE to 750 CE, named for the many woven baskets found at its sites.

chaco-culture-national-historical-park.name: Chaco Canyon
chaco-culture-national-historical-park.summary: A remote New Mexico canyon that was a major Ancestral Puebloan cultural center from 900 to 1150, where large stone complexes were built before drought led to abandonment.

kiva.name: Kiva
kiva.summary: An underground room used by Puebloans for spiritual ceremonies, worship and political meetings, evolved from earlier pit-houses and found among ancient ruins across the Southwestern United States.

ancestral-puebloans.name: Ancestral Puebloans
ancestral-puebloans.summary: An ancient Native American culture spanning the Four Corners region of the US, living in pit houses, clan structures and cliff dwellings, linked by a network of communities across the Colorado Plateau.

monks-mound.name: Monks Mound
monks-mound.summary: The largest prehistoric earthwork in the Americas, built from about 900 to 955 CE at Cahokia in Illinois, with a base roughly as large as the Great Pyramid of Giza.

pueblo-bonito.name: Pueblo Bonito
pueblo-bonito.summary: The largest and best-known great house in Chaco Canyon, New Mexico, built and occupied by Ancestral Puebloans between about 828 and 1126, called an archaeological icon on par with Stonehenge or Machu Picchu.

alligator-effigy-mound.name: Alligator Effigy Mound
alligator-effigy-mound.summary: Ceremonial earthwork in Granville, Ohio, built between AD 800 and 1200 by the Fort Ancient culture, one of only two surviving effigy mounds in the state.

brad-lepper.name: Brad Lepper
brad-lepper.summary: American archaeologist known for work on ancient earthworks and ice age peoples in Ohio, and curator of archaeology at the Ohio History Connection.

underwater-panther.name: Underwater panther
underwater-panther.summary: Mythical water being of Indigenous peoples of the Great Lakes region, especially the Anishinaabeg, depicted as a scaled, spiked feline and considered a powerful underworld figure.

caddoan-mississippian-culture.name: Caddoan Mississippian culture
caddoan-mississippian-culture.summary: A prehistoric Native American culture, a variant of the Mississippian culture, spanning what is now Oklahoma, Arkansas, Texas and Louisiana, and ancestral to the modern Caddo Nation.

four-corners.name: Four Corners
four-corners.summary: A region of the southwestern US where Colorado, Utah, Arizona and New Mexico meet, homeland of the Ancestral Puebloans.

woodland-period.name: Woodland period
woodland-period.summary: An archaeological period of pre-Columbian eastern North America lasting from about 1000 BCE to European contact, marked by continuous development and the spread of pottery.

platform-mound.name: Platform mound
platform-mound.summary: A flat-topped earthwork mound built to support a structure or elevate an activity.

hopewell-tradition.name: Hopewell tradition
hopewell-tradition.summary: A network of Native American cultures and trade routes, not a single society, that flourished along Eastern Woodlands rivers from 100 BCE to 500 CE, exchanging goods and ideas.

american-bottom.name: American Bottom
american-bottom.summary: The Mississippi River's flood plain in southern Illinois, once the center of the pre-Columbian Cahokia Mounds civilization.

tombigbee-river.name: Tombigbee River
tombigbee-river.summary: A roughly 200-mile river in Mississippi and Alabama that formed the eastern boundary of historical Choctaw lands before their forced removal in the 1830s.

pinson-mounds.name: Pinson Mounds
pinson-mounds.summary: A prehistoric Native American complex of 17 mounds in Tennessee, built around 1–500 AD and the largest group of Middle Woodland mounds in the United States.

cosmogram.name: cosmogram
cosmogram.summary: A flat schematic diagram, often built around a circle and a square or cross, used to represent the structure of the universe or earth according to a culture's worldview.

pueblo-i-period.name: Pueblo I period
pueblo-i-period.summary: An archaeological period, 750 to 900 CE, when Ancestral Puebloans first began living in pueblo structures, with evolving architecture, art and water conservation.

l-anse-aux-meadows.name: L'Anse aux Meadows
l-anse-aux-meadows.summary: A Norse settlement site on Newfoundland's northern tip, dated to around 1000 CE by carbon and tree-ring evidence, the only confirmed pre-Columbian European site in the Americas outside Greenland.

mesoamerican-ballcourt.name: Mesoamerican ballcourt
mesoamerican-ballcourt.summary: A large masonry structure used across Mesoamerica for over 2,700 years to play a ritual ball game, also serving as a site for feasts and public spectacle.

vinland.name: Vinland
vinland.summary: Area of coastal North America explored by Vikings, where Leif Erikson landed around AD 1000, long before Columbus; Norse building remains confirming it were found at L'Anse aux Meadows, Newfoundland, in 1960.

human-sacrifice.name: Retainer sacrifice
human-sacrifice.summary: The ritual killing of a monarch's or leader's servants upon their death, so they may continue to serve their master in the next life.
